newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK PSBR to show repayment in October.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK PSBR to show repayment in October.

text.p: UK public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) data on Monday are expected to show a net repayment in October due to an inflow of corporate tax receipts.
Reuters' consensus forecast is for a repayment of 1.6 billion stg after September's budget deficit of 3.4 billion, but some economists are more upbeat.

"We are optimistic surrounding the prospects for a favourable out-turn since this is an important month for corporation tax receipts, which have been flowing into the Exchequer at a brisk 16-1/2 percent above year-ago levels," said Philip Shaw, chief economist at Union Discount.
"This, plus some 200 million stg of privatisation proceeds...should result in a debt repayment of some 2.2 billion sterling," he said.
Economists at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said last month's PSBR was disappointing, with receipts growth below expectations.

"Nevertheless, with the economy accelerating, led by stronger consumer spending, receipts growth should be at least as high as government forecasts for the full fiscal year," they wrote in their weekly look ahead.
DMG puts the October repayment at 2.7 billion stg due to both corporation tax and around 700 million stg from the sale of Ministry of Defence housing.
October's PSBR figures will be the last before the November 26 budget, which looks set to be overshadowed by the looming general election.

Economists say further restraint on public spending will be needed in the coming months if the government is to meet its 27 billion stg target for the financial year to April 5 -- no mean feat in an election year.
But stronger economic growth should boost revenue in the months ahead.

"At the halfway point, the official PSBR forecast of 27 billion stg for 1996/97 is still in sight, but only just," said Jonathan Loynes of HSBC Markets, who says the main threat to the target is on the spending side.

He expects a rebound in departmental spending growth in October to just over 3.0 percent. Against that, corporation tax revenue should rise about four percent from a year earlier and privatisation proceeds should total around 200 million stg.
"We expect a public sector debt repayment of 1-1/2 billion stg in October or 1.3 billion excluding privatisation proceeds," he said.
"This would leave a cumulative ex-privatisation proceeds deficit of 18.5 billion stg, just 1/2 billion stg lower than at the same stage of last year."
